summary: Set up native filesystem-snapshot/rollback for /srv/data on node1 (Alpine, ext4 root has no native snapshot support) by installing btrfs-progs, creating a loopback-backed btrfs filesystem with a 'data' subvolume mounted at /srv/data (persisted via /etc/fstab). Populated /srv/data with app files, took a read-only btrfs snapshot as baseline, modified the live directory (edit/delete/add), then restored /srv/data to the exact baseline snapshot content via subvolume swap, verified byte-identical via sha256 manifest diff. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and data checksums, rebooted node1, polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime, and re-verified /srv/data auto-remounted with content still matching the baseline manifest.
actions_performed: Installed btrfs-progs and loaded btrfs kernel module on node1
Created 2GiB loopback image, formatted btrfs, created 'data' subvolume, mounted at /srv/data
Persisted mount via /etc/fstab (loop,subvol=data) and added btrfs to /etc/modules so it survives reboot
Populated /srv/data with app/config/app.conf and app/uploads/record1.txt, record2.txt
Took read-only btrfs snapshot of /srv/data as baseline; saved sha256 manifest
Modified /srv/data (edited app.conf, deleted record2.txt, added junk.txt) confirming drift via manifest diff
Restored /srv/data to exact baseline snapshot via subvolume swap (mv corrupted subvol aside, snapshot baseline as new 'data' subvol, remount); verified byte-identical via sha256 diff
Captured pre-restart boot_id and data health proof
Issued native reboot on node1, polled until exec available again
Confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime post-restart
Re-verified /srv/data auto-mounted via fstab post-reboot with content matching baseline manifest exactly

evidence.requirement: Filesystem snapshot capability established for /srv/data (btrfs subvolume + loop-mounted fs)
evidence.summary: btrfs-progs installed, btrfs module loaded, loopback device formatted as btrfs with a 'data' subvolume mounted at /srv/data, persisted via /etc/fstab and confirmed via mount -a

evidence.requirement: Baseline data populated and snapshot captured
evidence.summary: Created app.conf, record1.txt, record2.txt under /srv/data, recorded sha256 checksums, then created a read-only btrfs snapshot and confirmed its content matches the live data manifest
app.conf overwritten, record2.txt deleted, junk.txt added; diff against baseline manifest shows the drift

evidence.requirement: Exact restore of earlier snapshot content
evidence.summary: Live subvolume swapped for a writable snapshot of the read-only baseline snapshot; post-restore sha256 manifest diff against baseline manifest is empty (byte-identical), junk.txt gone, record2.txt and app.conf restored

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 7d560aac-09ed-4407-810c-51eb86900733, uptime start, fstab entry, live mount, file listing, checksums, and btrfs subvolume list prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent polls show connection reset/timeout during restart, then exec succeeds again with a new boot_id (e59ae8ad-d30a-46a7-a66a-eb2c07e8d4ab) and fresh uptime start (23:02:00), proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/data and its content verified
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data auto-mounted via fstab (btrfs subvol=data), btrfs module auto-loaded, file listing and sha256 manifest diff against the baseline manifest show zero differences, and both the baseline snapshot and corrupted-data subvolume persisted on disk
